Please review the following manuscript I wrote.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-f01oc86q/call-540c249932ce46299fa9e056e5ebc76c/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la; ls -l manuscript.pdf; command -v pdftotext; command -v pdfinfo; command -v pdftoppm; command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs; python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text()
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n===== PAGE {i} =====\\n{t}')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:4]))
PY"
/bin/bash -c 'cat tmp/pdfs/page-08.txt tmp/pdfs/page-09.txt tmp/pdfs/page-10.txt tmp/pdfs/page-11.txt tmp/pdfs/page-12.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt'

strengths: The task is practically motivated: combining a reference person image with a description of changed attributes addresses limitations of image-only and text-only retrieval. ITCPR provides a potentially useful benchmark with 2,202 queries and 20,510 gallery images.

The two-stage framework is straightforward and avoids composed-query training triplets by using existing identity-labeled image-caption data. Freezing the encoders during textual inversion training makes the additional model lightweight.

Reported improvements are substantial across both backbones. In Table 1, the best ViT-L/14 configuration achieves 45.91% Rank-1 and 55.63% mAP, compared with 35.38% and 44.08% for the strongest listed baseline on these metrics.

The supplementary experiments add useful evidence through loss comparisons, training-data scaling, and inference timing. Table B supports identity-aware matching over instance-level contrastive learning, while the qualitative analysis suggests an interesting distinction between visual and semantic supervision.
weaknesses: The main comparisons do not adequately isolate the methodological contribution. Pic2Word and SEARLE retain mappings trained with original CLIP, including when evaluated with fine-tuned encoders; the manuscript itself acknowledges this mismatch. These methods should also be adapted using matched encoders and training data. Table B partially addresses this concern, showing approximately three percentage points from the loss change, but does not replace matched comparisons under the main ViT-L/14 setting.

The evaluation does not establish an independent model-selection protocol. Section 4 designates ITCPR exclusively for testing, yet Section 5.3 selects network architecture and prompt configuration using its results. Without a separate validation procedure, reported performance risks reflecting test-set tuning. Triplet-free training is supported, but untouched-test generalization is insufficiently established.

Methodological originality is limited relative to the cited work: the framework combines established person-retrieval fine-tuning, image-to-pseudo-word mapping, and matching losses. The strongest original contribution is the task and benchmark. The manuscript needs a sharper account of what person-specific insight extends existing zero-shot composed image retrieval.

Benchmark reliability and coverage need stronger evidence. Appendix B.1 screens potential additional positives using an unspecified visual encoder and top-k cutoff, without quantifying remaining annotation errors. Annotation agreement and results by source dataset or modification type are absent. Selecting pairs with partially shared clothing also limits the scope of conclusions about broader clothes-changing retrieval.

Important reporting ambiguities affect reproducibility and interpretation. Table 1 labels the combined configuration as L_vis + L_text, whereas Appendix C.4 discusses these results as fusion of separately trained networks; joint optimization and inference ensembling should be distinguished explicitly. No variation across runs or confidence intervals is reported, making the smaller prompt and fusion improvements difficult to assess.

The proposed benchmark and public-security motivation warrant documentation of image reuse and redistribution permissions, privacy considerations, and potential harms from surveillance or mistaken identification. These issues are not addressed; public availability of the source datasets alone does not resolve them.
